review_notes: I read the complete target file (lines 1–201) and inspected the closest existing declarations in Mathlib: Mathlib/Data/Finset/Finsupp.lean (Finset.finsupp, Finsupp.pi, mem_finsupp_iff, mem_finsupp_iff_of_support_subset, card_finsupp, card_pi), Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Interval.lean (Finsupp.rangeSingleton, Finsupp.rangeIcc, instLocallyFiniteOrder, Icc_eq, card_Icc/Ico/Ioc/Ioo, card_uIcc, card_Iic/Iio), Mathlib/Data/Pi/Interval.lean, Mathlib/Data/Finset/Pi.lean, Mathlib/Data/Fintype/Pi.lean, Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Defs.lean, Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Sigma.lean, Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Order.lean, Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/ToDFinsupp.lean, and searched Batteries and Lean core for DFinsupp/Finsupp notions (none found). The nearest candidates are the Finsupp parallels: Finset.dfinsupp vs Finset.finsupp, DFinsupp.pi vs Finsupp.pi, DFinsupp.singleton vs Finsupp.rangeSingleton, DFinsupp.rangeIcc vs Finsupp.rangeIcc, and the two LocallyFiniteOrder instances with their cardinality lemmas. I did not treat these as findings: the target declarations are dependent DFinsupp constructions (Π₀ i, α i) while the existing ones are constant-fibre Finsupp constructions (ι →₀ α), a deliberately different representation documented in Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Defs.lean lines 40–44 and bridged by finsuppEquivDFinsupp. The target versions are the strictly more general constructions needed for dependent α, not avoidable copies of an existing declaration; deriving the older Finsupp API from them would be a refactor of the older files with unclear defeq and maintenance benefits, so the practical case for consolidation is unclear and the rubric directs abstention. The one naming divergence, DFinsupp.singleton versus Finsupp.rangeSingleton, is a consistency observation rather than a substantive duplication: neither declaration is used elsewhere, and the dependent construction is not obtainable from the nondependent one for arbitrary dependent fibres. Within the file, DFinsupp.pi is a named specialisation of Finset.dfinsupp, and mem_singleton_apply_iff, mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff and rangeIcc_apply restate mem_singleton, mem_Icc and rfl; the rubric explicitly excludes standalone theorem duplication and named specialisations. Remaining uncertainty: I could not compile a proposed bridge between Finset.dfinsupp and Finset.finsupp, so the judgement that such a refactor is not clearly beneficial is informal.
